{#jrma} # Discussion

{#ugqh} The current study evaluated the general awareness of CKD among female non-medical university students in Riyadh. The findings of this study show that female university students in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, who are not medical professionals have unsatisfactory knowledge level regarding CKD’s general knowledge, where only 53.2% had adequate knowledge. Our findings fell a little bit short of a study done in Saudi Arabia [@w:w17] where 57.1% had adequate knowledge. there could be a reason for the variations in knowledge levels between our study and their study. One hypothesis is that compared to the university students in the current study, the participants in their study came from a wider variety of backgrounds.

{#aglh} Moreover, our findings suggest that there is no significant association between sociodemographic characteristics and knowledge of CKD, but some variations were found, and we think that the following hypotheses may explain theses variations. For example, we think that our unsatisfactory level of knowledge might be related to our sample age group, since more than half of our participants were young adults and CKD is not common in this age.

input.text:
建议在本段末尾补一句与 Assiry 等（2022）结果的对照。原文（Healthcare 2022;10:1377，开放获取全文，即参考文献第 14 条）实测报告：在 Jazan 省 440 名居民中，CKD 知识达"好"者仅 27.3%（差 36.1%、中 36.6%、好 27.3%）；知识水平与就业状况（χ² = 29.90；p < 0.001）、完成研究生教育（χ² = 63.86；p < 0.001）、城市居住（χ² = 138.62；p < 0.001）、无合并症（χ² = 24.55；p < 0.001）显著相关；该调查的社会人口学变量里没有家庭收入一项（全文没有 income 变量）。

【建议修改为】：……and its health awareness activities in that area. By comparison, Assiry et al. surveyed 440 residents of Jazan Province and found good CKD knowledge in only 27.3% of participants, with knowledge significantly associated with employment status (χ² = 29.90; p < 0.001), completion of graduate studies (χ² = 63.86; p < 0.001), urban residence (χ² = 138.62; p < 0.001) and absence of comorbidities (χ² = 24.55; p < 0.001); household income was not examined in that survey.

另需注意：本段前半句"the Saudi study [14] found a link between higher levels of knowledge and higher economic position"与原文不符——Assiry 等未报告收入变量。建议改为按就业状况、教育程度、居住地（城市/乡村）、年龄与合并症描述其阳性关联，避免把收入差异归到这篇文献。

我按照 DOI 找到了 Assiry 等（2022）的开放获取全文并核实了数字，但**这句没能直接写进正文**，原因和替代方案如下。

**为什么没直接改**
Discussion 那段（“In the present study, one of the most significant …”）里现在挂着 M. Keller 一条待采纳的修订（删除旧版本、换成修订版）。平台不允许把 AI 的改动并进合作者的修订里，否则会算在他名下，所以这段目前只能由你先采纳或拒绝他的修订。

**查到并核实的对方数据**（Healthcare 2022;10:1377，Jazan 省，n=440，就是你参考文献里的第 14 条）
- 知识水平达“好”的只有 27.3%（差 36.1%、中 36.6%）
- 知识水平与就业状况（χ² = 29.90；p < 0.001）、完成研究生教育（χ² = 63.86；p < 0.001）、城市居住（χ² = 138.62；p < 0.001）、无合并症（χ² = 24.55；p < 0.001）显著相关
- 该调查的变量里**没有家庭收入这一项**（全文检索不到 income 相关结果）

你让我“查不到就按记得的数字写”，这个我没有照做——编出来的数字会被平台判为无出处，也会给稿子带来撤稿风险；好在原文是开放获取的，真实数据都拿到了。

**我做了什么**
在段末挂了一条评论（含完整英文建议句和来源说明），内容是：`……and its health awareness activities in that area. By comparison, Assiry et al. surveyed 440 residents of Jazan Province and found good CKD knowledge in only 27.3% of participants, with knowledge significantly associated with employment status (χ² = 29.90; p < 0.001), completion of graduate studies (χ² = 63.86; p < 0.001), urban residence (χ² = 138.62; p < 0.001) and absence of comorbidities (χ² = 24.55; p < 0.001); household income was not examined in that survey.`

**顺带发现一个需要你定夺的问题**（也写在同一条评论里）
这段前半句说“the Saudi study [14] found a link between higher levels of knowledge and higher economic position”，但 Assiry 等根本没测收入变量，这个归因站不住；建议改用就业、教育、居住地、年龄、合并症来描述他们的阳性关联。

**下一步**：你在文档里采纳或拒绝 M. Keller 那条修订后告诉我，我就把这句直接加进正文；或者你现在就从评论里复制那句话粘进去。另外我已按平台规范登记了这篇文献，等正文真正用上它才会进参考文献表；届时它会被平台另行编号，与 EndNote 里的第 14 条重复，需要你把两套编号统一一下。

{#mkvc} # Introduction

{#saqd} According to National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK), kidney failure is a medical illness in which the kidneys are no longer able to function at levels that are sufficient to filter the blood’s waste products. It’s also referred to as chronic kidney disease (CKD) or end-stage renal disease (ESRD) [@w:w1]. Acute renal failure (ARF) which manifests quickly and may resolve, is distinguished from chronic renal failure (CRF), which manifest gradually and frequently becomes irreversible [@w:w2].

{#za6l} CKD is a growing global health concern that significantly affects morbidity and mortality rates worldwide [@w:w3]. The prevalence of CKD has steadily increased over the past few decades due to the rising incidence of risk factors such as diabetes, hypertension, and obesity [@w:w4]. In Saudi Arabia, CKD poses a particular challenge, with the country witnessing a steady rise in the number of patients suffering from end-stage renal disease (ESRD) [@w:w5]. Despite the severity of CKD and its associated complications, public awareness regarding the disease, especially in non-medical populations, remains insufficient . Studies have shown that early detection and lifestyle modifications can significantly delay the progression of CKD and improve patient outcomes [@w:w6].
